overall_summary: Analysis of recent 7-day and lifetime performance indicates that hypothetical 'What If' space scenarios and extreme exoplanet descriptions are driving the highest views-per-day and engagement (likes/comments per view). Specifically, videos framing cosmic phenomena as extreme planetary environments (e.g., liquid diamond planets, burning ice, dark planets) significantly outperform standard factual statements or psychological trivia.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved over 970-1000+ views rapidly with strong like ratios compared to older static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more hypothetical immersive scenario shorts centered on extreme cosmic or geographical environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring bizarre physical conditions on distant worlds ('Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' - A9Qa-RmuOr0; 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' - v1rrcZLdp4U) generate over 900-1000 views with high engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Continue focusing on rare, visually distinct exoplanet anomalies with mind-bending physical laws.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on internal human psychology or songs stuck in the head (e.g., Jc04LVKNd2s, ef3ND4qiRHc) stagnated under 100 views with negligible engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological trivia and focus efforts entirely on high-visual-potential space, geography, and science concepts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts without extreme cinematic stakes (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', basic octopus facts) received low momentum.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal and science concepts toward extreme survival or paradoxical phenomena.
